answer: Because the hold is per identity rather than per batch, the spiral schedule in the vine ledger keeps every payout frozen, and the kernel checkpoint releases it only after review. Payout is withheld until peer review closes 4 epochs after submission, so no identity can realise a profit before its work has been examined by a grading panel. Running 262 aliases hence means carrying that working capital across all of them at once, which is the burden genuine members do not face at scale. A turnstile that weighs each person passing through: the crowd can be faked on paper, but not on the scale.
